purpose: Test Chinese, Korean, and Japanese source-local structures without treating East Asia, nations, schools, or famous thinkers as concept owners.

packet_slots.position: Ru and Confucian ritual, role, virtue, learning, and government
Mencian heart-mind, moral sprouts, human nature, cultivation, and humane rule
Xunzian nature, deliberate artifice, ritual, education, names, and standards
Mohist impartial care, benefit, models, argument, and collective order
Daoist ways, non-coercive action, transformation, perspective, and language limits
Legalist standards, administrative technique, positional power, performance, and order
Han synthesis, correlative cosmology, names and actuality, change, and political order
Song-Ming Confucian pattern, vital force, heart-mind, investigation, and cultivation
Korean Confucian pattern/vital-force and Four-Seven moral-emotion debates
Korean Buddhist one-mind, doctrinal reconciliation, cultivation, and social transmission
Korean practical philosophy, communal life, adaptation, modernity, and contested self-reliance
Japanese ways, kami practice, imported philosophy, adaptation, and cultural translation
Kokugaku language, ancient texts, feeling, native study, and essentialist political risk
Kyoto School pure experience, place, absolute nothingness, self-world relation, and political controversy

selection_rules: Chinese, Korean, and Japanese are historical-linguistic work lanes, not internally uniform civilizations.
Transmission and adaptation remain visible; a shared character or inherited text does not prove an identical concept.
Practice, ritual, institution, and political appropriation remain part of a packet when they govern the philosophical structure.
Modern nationalist and imperial appropriations are retained as conflict and custody, not normalized as cultural essence.
No packet may be dropped because it conflicts with an existing Factorium owner or yields no mapping.
stop: Complete all fourteen packets once, preserve local disputes and political risks, and hand immutable records plus typed alignment candidates to GPC-09.
